_about: Hand-picked corrections applied on top of harvest's fuzzy match. Sources are named by any unique piece of their path, so this file stays readable and fails loudly if the collections move. 'image' = mount the whole disk; 'file' = [source, FILENAME ON THAT DISK]; 'unavailable' = nothing in the local cache is this game. by_title applies wherever the title appears; by_side overrides one side only.

B.C.'s Quest for Tires.note: the single-file hit named "BC'S QUEST II" turned out on screen to be B.C. II: Grog's Revenge

Mystery at Pinecrest Manor.note: PINECREST MANOR on its own is a story file, not a program - it needs Scholastic's Tales of Mystery engine, so the whole side goes on

Dino Eggs.note: the file on the disk loads at $0400, over screen memory - it is a loader stage, not the game

Rambo: First Blood Part II.note: fuzzy match picked Rambo III; only the Ocean original is in the cache

Battlezone.note: Hotline crack; the earlier pick was an unrelated disk called battle.d64

Jungle Hunt.note: fetched from the Internet Archive's C64 library (Atari, 1984)

Pitfall!.note: the PITFAL file found sits on a Game Maker sampler

Bruce Lee.note: every single-file hit was a copier parameter

River Raid.note: the only single file found was River Raid II

H.E.R.O..note: fetched from the Internet Archive - the Spanish Load 'n' Run release; same game, Spanish title screen

Monster Smash.note: the MONSTERS file found was from Dragons of Flame

Ghost Manor.note: side 2 of the Xonox double-ender - side 1 is Spike's Peak; the single-file hit was a Kracker Jax parameter

Sublogic Football.note: fetched from the Internet Archive; multi-file, so the whole side goes on

Blue Thunder.note: the disk holds a 1-block loader; it needs the whole image

Agent USA.note: the 23-block hit was Agent U.O.P., a different game

Boulder Dash II.note: SUBSTITUTE - Boulder Dash II (Rockford's Riot) is not in the cache, this is the first game

Gauntlet: The Deeper Dungeons.note: the draft reused the plain Gauntlet disk

Up'n Down.note: the earlier pick was Upside Down, a different game

Danger Mouse in the Black Forest Chateau.note: fetched from the Internet Archive (Creative Sparks, 1984); loads in two parts, so the whole side goes on

Lode Runner.note: the earlier pick was Road Runner

Stellar 7.note: the disk file was a 1-block loader

Bagitman.note: fetched from the Internet Archive (Aardvark, 1984) - the label says SYS 16384, which the build works out from the file itself

Gyruss.note: fetched from the Internet Archive - the Spanish Load 'n' Run release of the Parker Brothers game

The Game Show.note: fetched from the Internet Archive (Advanced Ideas, 1984); multi-file, so the whole side goes on

Genesis.note: everything else matching 'genesis' was the Genesis Project cracking group

Big Top Barney.note: fetched from the Internet Archive (Interceptor Micros, 1984)

World Karate Championship.note: Eagle Soft crack, multi-file (LDR + GAME.A/B) so it needs the whole side; the KARATE CHAMP hit is Data East's Karate Champ, a different game

Centropods.note: UNCONFIRMED - a Centipede-style game on a Keypunch compilation

Moon Patrol.note: UNCONFIRMED - the file sits on a disk labelled Tomahawk

Caveman.unavailable: still not found - the archive's 'Caveman' is a 1990 Compute! type-in and 'Crazy Caveman' does not look like the arcade game

Rad Skater.note: SUBSTITUTE - no C64 game is called Rad Skater; Skate or Die (EA, 1987) is the likeliest thing the label meant

Time Pilot.unavailable: no C64 release found anywhere - the arcade game was never ported to the 64; the label may mean a clone

Hey Diddle Diddle.note: fetched from the Internet Archive (Spinnaker, 1983); multi-file, so the whole side goes on

Mario's Brewery.note: fetched from the Internet Archive (Mr. Computer, 1983)
